# Synapse 2.0.15

Synapse AI reads a Vault file you ask about, two runs adding to the same Vault file at the same moment keep every line, even when one of them creates the file in that moment, and pages behind Cloudflare and other bot managers are no longer reported as blocked when they loaded fine.

## Fixed

- **Synapse AI reads a Vault file you ask about.** Asked to summarise a file in your Vault, or to answer from it, Synapse AI said it could not read Vault files. It now reads the file you name, by its name, its path or an @ mention, and answers from it, without ever changing it. It reads up to 20,000 characters of a file and says so when a file is longer; a file it cannot read, or a name two files share, is said, and it asks which one you mean.
- **Two runs adding to the same Vault file at the same moment never lose a line, including when one of them creates the file in that moment.** Adding to a Vault file was already safe when two runs added at once, but a run could still write over a file another run had just created, or changed while it was reading it. A run now reads the file again in that case, so every line is kept.
- **Pages behind Cloudflare are no longer reported as blocked when they loaded fine.** Reading a web page could say "Blocked by anti-bot protection" for a page that had loaded in full, because Cloudflare, PerimeterX and Imperva put a small script on every page they watch. A page is now reported as blocked only when the site actually showed a challenge, a captcha or a refusal, and the message names whose block it was.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.15`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.x:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
